A Balanced Attack

The backfield runs through one man — Kyren Williams absorbs 68% of the carries (league ~59%), a true bell-cow share that makes his rushing volume among the safest floors in the sport when the script cooperates.

The Offensive Blueprint

They're a heavy under-center team (48% shotgun vs ~68%) — a pro-style, run-committed structure.

They run downhill — mostly inside the tackles (18% to the edge vs ~25%), a gap/power scheme that trades big plays for a steady, grinding floor.

LA throw by design. They pass -0% over expectation (league -2%) and keep firing even with a lead (44% early-down pass when ahead vs ~41%) — the kind of pass-first identity that keeps receivers live in every script.

The tight end is barely used in the passing game (9% of targets vs ~15%) — fade their TE's receiving props.

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 19% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

By the numbers it's an efficient unit — a 49% success rate (above the 44% average).

They push it downfield — average depth of target 8.6 yards with 23% of throws traveling 15+, a vertical passing game that trades completions for boom-or-bust yardage.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they stay aggressive, throwing 55% of the time, which puts scoring equity on Puka Nacua.

Defense — The Run Comes Free

Soft against opposing WR1s — 68 rec yds/game (vs ~58). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 124 rushing and 239 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

Soft against opposing tight ends — 41 rec yds/game (vs ~35). A rec-yards target.

Soft against backs out of the backfield — 23 rec yds/game (vs ~18). A rec-yards target.

They leak WR1 receiving TDs (0.59/game vs ~0.38) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
